To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) CRM performance is affected by the degree of alignment of CRM activities according to strategy, monitoring and controls, organization and processes and IT, and (ii) CRM performance is additionally affected by the degree to which CRM activities are aligned across the four CRM areas: customer insight, customer interaction, customer contact, marketing.
CRM alignment is positively related to CRM performance and that CRM integration is positively related to alignment.
CRM performance is positively influenced by the alignment of CRM activities according to both business dimensions and CRM areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how organizations can achieve CRM performance by aligning their CRM activities according to a number of business dimensions.
the alignment of CRM activities in relation to business dimensions and CRM areas.
the question of why some organizations are able to achieve CRM performance, while others do not.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more CRM activities are aligned according to the dimensions of business alignment, the better the performance of the CRM initiative.

organizations that have a well-defined and integrated CRM strategy, that have a clear vision on the use of customer insight, that have an integrated approach to customer contact, and that are well aligned on all business dimensions, are most likely to be successful in the CRM arena.
the CRM performance of organizations can be enhanced by aligning their CRM strategy and activities with the five business dimensions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRM alignment framework provides a valuable tool for organizations in the CRM domain to assess and improve their CRM performance.
CRM performance is a function of the alignment of the CRM activities according to the business dimensions and the integration of the CRM areas.
the alignment of CRM activities in the five business dimensions and the four CRM areas is a critical success factors for organizations that embark on CRM initiatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRM is not a single, isolated concept but that CRM is a combination of several activities that are all interrelated.
organizations need to focus on both the CRM and business alignment dimensions.
CRM alignment is not only about the CRM system, but also about the business processes, organizational structures, employees, and culture.
